claims.title: First recorded sighting
claims.summary: The English navigator John Davis is credited with the first recorded European sighting of the uninhabited islands; the territory marks Falklands Day on 14 August in commemoration.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Falkland Islands: A wind-scoured South Atlantic archipelago — the Falkland Islands to the United Kingdom, Islas Malvinas to Argentina — whose contested sovereignty, a long pastoral colony, a 1982 war and an overwhelming 2013 referendum have made it one of the world's most closely watched disputed territories.", terralore.co/country/FLK/chronicle#ev-1592-first-recorded-sighting, claim TL:FLK:event:1592:first-recorded-sighting, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: French Port Louis founded
claims.summary: Louis-Antoine de Bougainville established the first settlement, Port Louis, on East Falkland, and named the islands the Malouines — origin of the Spanish Malvinas.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Falkland Islands: A wind-scoured South Atlantic archipelago — the Falkland Islands to the United Kingdom, Islas Malvinas to Argentina — whose contested sovereignty, a long pastoral colony, a 1982 war and an overwhelming 2013 referendum have made it one of the world's most closely watched disputed territories.", terralore.co/country/FLK/chronicle#ev-1764-french-port-louis-founded, claim TL:FLK:event:1764:french-port-louis-founded, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British Port Egmont established
claims.summary: A British expedition under Commodore John Byron claimed West Falkland in 1765, and Britain founded Port Egmont on Saunders Island the following year.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Falkland Islands: A wind-scoured South Atlantic archipelago — the Falkland Islands to the United Kingdom, Islas Malvinas to Argentina — whose contested sovereignty, a long pastoral colony, a 1982 war and an overwhelming 2013 referendum have made it one of the world's most closely watched disputed territories.", terralore.co/country/FLK/chronicle#ev-1765-british-port-egmont-established, claim TL:FLK:event:1765:british-port-egmont-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Spain buys out the French and administers from Buenos Aires
claims.summary: Spain purchased the French settlement around 1767 and governed the islands from Buenos Aires; in 1770 it expelled the British from Port Egmont, restored after a 1771 settlement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Falkland Islands: A wind-scoured South Atlantic archipelago — the Falkland Islands to the United Kingdom, Islas Malvinas to Argentina — whose contested sovereignty, a long pastoral colony, a 1982 war and an overwhelming 2013 referendum have made it one of the world's most closely watched disputed territories.", terralore.co/country/FLK/chronicle#ev-1767-spain-buys-out-the-french-and-administers-from, claim TL:FLK:event:1767:spain-buys-out-the-french-and-administers-from, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Buenos Aires proclaims sovereignty
claims.summary: Having declared independence from Spain in 1816, the Buenos Aires government proclaimed its sovereignty over the islands, the basis of Argentina's later claim.

claims.title: USS Lexington raid on Port Louis
claims.summary: The U.S. warship Lexington destroyed the Argentine settlement on East Falkland in reprisal for the seizure of American sealing ships, ending Vernet's colony.

claims.title: Britain re-establishes control (founding of continuous administration)
claims.summary: A British force required the small Argentine garrison to leave Port Louis and re-asserted British control — the start of continuous British administration, which Argentina contests as illegitimate occupation.

claims.summary: Britain appointed a civilian lieutenant governor for the Falklands, formalising the colonial administration begun in 1833.

claims.title: Stanley becomes the capital
claims.summary: The seat of government moved to Stanley on East Falkland, which became the islands' capital, port and main settlement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Falkland Islands: A wind-scoured South Atlantic archipelago — the Falkland Islands to the United Kingdom, Islas Malvinas to Argentina — whose contested sovereignty, a long pastoral colony, a 1982 war and an overwhelming 2013 referendum have made it one of the world's most closely watched disputed territories.", terralore.co/country/FLK/chronicle#ev-1845-stanley-becomes-the-capital, claim TL:FLK:event:1845:stanley-becomes-the-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Falkland Islands Company chartered
claims.summary: The Falkland Islands Company received a royal charter in 1851 and grew into the colony's largest landowner and sheep rancher, central to its wool economy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Falkland Islands: A wind-scoured South Atlantic archipelago — the Falkland Islands to the United Kingdom, Islas Malvinas to Argentina — whose contested sovereignty, a long pastoral colony, a 1982 war and an overwhelming 2013 referendum have made it one of the world's most closely watched disputed territories.", terralore.co/country/FLK/chronicle#ev-1851-falkland-islands-company-chartered, claim TL:FLK:event:1851:falkland-islands-company-chartered, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: A self-supporting wool colony
claims.summary: By 1885 a British community of some 1,800 people on the islands was self-supporting, sustained mainly by sheep farming and wool exports.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Falkland Islands: A wind-scoured South Atlantic archipelago — the Falkland Islands to the United Kingdom, Islas Malvinas to Argentina — whose contested sovereignty, a long pastoral colony, a 1982 war and an overwhelming 2013 referendum have made it one of the world's most closely watched disputed territories.", terralore.co/country/FLK/chronicle#ev-1885-a-self-supporting-wool-colony, claim TL:FLK:event:1885:a-self-supporting-wool-colony, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of the Falkland Islands
claims.summary: A British naval squadron destroyed a German cruiser force off the islands in an early First World War engagement, underscoring their strategic position near Cape Horn.

claims.title: Listed as a Non-Self-Governing Territory
claims.summary: The Falkland Islands (Malvinas) were placed on the UN list of Non-Self-Governing Territories after the UK transmitted information under Article 73(e) of the Charter.

claims.title: British landings at San Carlos
claims.summary: British forces landed at San Carlos on East Falkland and advanced overland, capturing Darwin and Goose Green before closing on Stanley.

claims.summary: Argentine forces surrendered at Stanley after a 74-day campaign; about 255 British and 649 Argentine personnel and three islanders died in the war.

claims.title: Security Council Resolution 502
claims.summary: The Council determines that a breach of the peace exists, calls for an immediate cessation of hostilities, demands the prompt withdrawal of all Argentine forces, and urges both governments to seek a diplomatic settlement under the Charter. Adopted 10 in favour, 1 against, 4 abstentions.

claims.title: The Commons sits on a Saturday
claims.summary: Parliament meets on a Saturday for the first time in a generation. Margaret Thatcher opens by telling the House that, for the first time in many years, British sovereign territory has been invaded by a foreign power.

claims.summary: The Falkland Islands government created a fisheries conservation and licensing zone; squid licensing revenue became the mainstay of the post-war economy.

claims.title: Sovereignty referendum
claims.summary: About 99.8% of islanders voting (turnout c. 92%) chose to remain a British Overseas Territory; the UK upheld the result while Argentina rejected its validity.
